newsitem.title: USA: Fla. driver dies, 3 girls critical in train smash.
newsitem.headline: Fla. driver dies, 3 girls critical in train smash.

text.p: Three Florida children were in critical condition on Thursday after a car tried to beat a freight train through an intersection, was struck by the train and spun into them, police said.

The driver of the car, Thelma Roach, 78, was killed, police said. The girls -- LoRonda Waters, 10, LaKeonte Waters, 9, and Colisha Williams, 3 -- suffered severe head injuries and were rushed to central Florida hospitals.
Their mother, Celissa Waters, was in her kitchen early Wednesday evening and saw the accident. Her daughters had gone to a store across the street.
"I was standing at the window and I heard the train hit something," Waters told Reuters. "I thought it was an accident. Then when I looked up again I saw one of my children tumbling through the air."

Titusville police spokesman Jay Cullen said Roach drove her car under the train-crossing gates as they closed. The car stopped there, for unknown reasons, and the train sent it flipping onto the sidewalk where the girls were waiting to cross the street.
